title: Gen researchers say Remus stealer's Gmail interception uses a malicious Chrome extension, not a Gmail zero-day
date_note: The Gen post gives only its publication day (24 Nov); the Remus developers' promotion began 8 Nov, per Gen.
summary: Gen Threat Research says the Remus infostealer's new email interception feature installs a malicious Chrome extension, disguised as Google Sheets, that checks for new Gmail messages every minute and sends sender, subject and text to the attacker. The developers claimed a Gmail zero-day that survives password changes; Gen says it found no vulnerability and the extension does not bypass password changes or session revocation. The post does not mention a Google response.
plain: Gen says a data-stealing program's claimed Gmail 'zero-day' is really a malicious browser extension that keeps reading mail until it is removed, even after a password change.
exec: Gen says the claimed Gmail zero-day is a malicious Chrome extension; changing a password alone may not remove it.
action: General advice: check chrome://extensions for unfamiliar extensions and remove them after a password change; Gen's post lists hashes and extension IDs for hunting.
impact: Gen says the feature appears only in some Remus builds.

validation.note: Only Gen's own research post was read; no second publisher yet.
